title: fscale doctor --json output
description: What `fscale doctor --json` prints: whether this machine is ready for the repo. Paths are relative to the repo root with forward slashes. Values of env variables, passwords and connection strings never appear.

schemaVersion.description: Version of this format. Changes only on a breaking change.

ok.description: True when no check found a problem. Warnings do not count. The exit code is 0 when true, 1 when false.

problems.description: How many checks have the status problem.

warnings.description: How many checks have the status warning.

checks.description: Every check, grouped by section in the order tools, env, dependencies, services.

section.description: tools: installed tool versions against what the repo declares. env: the names in each .env.example. dependencies: installed packages and virtual environments. services: local services the repo names.

project.description: The folder of the project the check is about, as fscale facts prints it. Absent for checks about the whole repo.

subject.description: What was checked, such as node, pnpm, backend/.env.example or PostgreSQL on localhost:5432.

status.description: ok, problem (fscale doctor exits 1) or warning (worth a look, not wrong for certain).

detail.description: One sentence on what was found. Names of variables, never their values.

fix.description: The command or step that fixes a problem or a warning.
